subject: Dressel is back, Marchand is hurting, and a 17-year-old just made history
preheader: Plus a 10-year-old breaking NAG records and today's aerobic freestyle set.

swimSet.title: Today's Swim Set
swimSet.description: A 3,000-yard aerobic freestyle builder where every interval has a specific focal cue -- your job is to stay present and steady, not just survive the yardage.

lift.title: Today's Lift
lift.description: A rotational core and anti-rotation stability session targeting the mid-body control that drives both freestyle and backstroke efficiency.

newsItems.title: Dressel delivers at US Nationals -- and he's not done yet
newsItems.body: Caeleb Dressel turned heads at US Nationals in Irvine with a 21.3/47.7 in the 50 and 100 free and a 22.8/50.4 in the 50 and 100 fly. In a full interview with SwimSwam, he reflected on the meet and previewed an upcoming training stint with Herbie Behm -- a pairing worth keeping an eye on.

newsItems.title: Marchand's hip flares up again before Euro Champs
newsItems.body: Leon Marchand has re-aggravated the same hip adductor injury that cut his French Nationals short, and he's now facing uncertainty about whether he'll contest the 400 IM at the 2026 European Championships. He says the call will be last-minute -- which is not the position anyone wants to be in heading into a major championship.

newsItems.title: 17-year-old Liberty Clark rewrites the record books
newsItems.body: Liberty Clark clocked a 24.28 in the 50 free at 2026 US Nationals to claim the 17-18 National Age Group record, taking it from Claire Curzan. It's her first long course NAG and her third overall -- and she's still 17.

newsItems.title: A 10-year-old just closed out his age group in historic fashion
newsItems.body: Gabriel Brown broke two long-course National Age Group records in the 10-and-under division at the Central Zone 14&U Championships in Evansville -- a remarkable send-off to the youngest age group in the sport. Remember the name.

athlete.name: Alex Walsh
athlete.photoCredit: Photo: Walsh Family, CC BY 2.5, via Wikimedia Commons
athlete.bio:
Alex Walsh is an American competitive swimmer born on July 31, 2001, in Nashville, Tennessee. Known for her versatility across all four strokes, she excelled in medley events from a young age, setting national age group records at 12 and leading her high school team to multiple state and national championships. She competed for the University of Virginia from 2020 to 2025.

Walsh's competitive achievements include three gold medals at the 2019 Pan American Games and a silver medal at the 2020 Olympic Games in the 200 m individual medley. She won 29 total medals across five NCAA Championships, including 23 golds, helping Virginia claim five team national titles. At the 2022 World Championships she won three golds, and she earned additional medals at multiple short course and long course World Championships through 2025.
